ep05007|haiku.final:
Action chosen: monitor (one work order submitted, status "work order submitted"). No speed step test and no inspection were run.

Diagnosis: the Tt alarm (72.1 C, limit 72.0) comes from high pump-room ambient, not from the thrust bearing or the RTD. Room ambient (P201.TT_ROOM) rose from 17.5 C (13 Oct, 03:37) to 28.2 C (14 Oct, 13:37). The maintenance log shows the room extraction fan VF-3 out of service since 10 Oct, with a work order (BT) still open.

Key evidence:
- Tt minus ambient stayed at 44 to 46 C for the whole 48 h window, and is 43.7 C now. Nominal is 44 +/- 2 C. A friction-driven rise would show Tt minus ambient climbing progressively, and it does not.
- Oil minus ambient is 25 to 31 C (nominal 29 +/- 3). Tr minus ambient is 35 to 40 C (nominal 38 +/- 2). Neither shows the oil-first signature of cooler fouling, or the pattern of a bearing problem.
- Speed (about 3540 rpm) and flow (about 397 m3/h) are constant, so there is no load change.
- Per manual section 7, ambient is checked first. With Tt minus ambient nominal, no pump fault is indicated.

Tests not run: a speed step test would cost production and could not change the decision. Tt minus ambient is already nominal, and the expected step response (about 6 C nominal versus 7 to 8 C for excess friction) is too small to separate reliably while ambient is still rising. A technician inspection costs about 8 h and money, and is not justified without an abnormal Tt minus ambient gap.

Work order text for the technician (French): "Alarme Tt P-201 causee par la chaleur ambiante du local de pompes (28 C, ventilateur d'extraction VF-3 en panne depuis le 10 oct.), et non par le palier de butee : Tt moins ambiante est nominal (44 a 46 C). Ne pas remplacer le palier ni le RTD. Accelerer la reparation du ventilateur VF-3 et surveiller Tt moins ambiante; intervenir si l'ecart depasse 48 C de facon soutenue."

Watch items for the caller: if Tt minus ambient stays above about 48 C, Tt diverges from ambient, or oil minus ambient exceeds 32 C, escalate to an inspection (IR and vibration on the thrust bearing, RTD loop check, oil cooler).

ep05008|sonnet.final:
**Action chosen:** replace_rtd (work order submitted, status "work order submitted").

**Diagnosis:** The thrust bearing RTD (P201.TT_THRUST) has drifted. The bearing itself is not overheating. The likely cause is moisture in the RTD junction box, which the maintenance log recorded on 2026-08-12 ("boite de jonction RTD butee trouvee humide, presse-etoupe resserre. A surveiller").

**Key evidence**
- Alarm: Tt 72.6 C against a 72.0 C limit, raised 2026-10-14 13:36.
- Ambient ruled out: the room is about 20 C. Tt minus room is now about 51.9 C, against a nominal 44 +/- 2 C, so this is not a hot-room alarm.
- Cooler ruled out: oil minus room is about 28 C (nominal 29 +/- 3). Tr minus oil stays near 9 C. The cooler model says Tt rises only about 0.45 C per C of oil rise, so the oil change cannot explain a Tt excess of about 7 C.
- Telemetry could not separate the two remaining causes. Tt has ramped about 0.4 C/h for roughly 20 h. A real friction increase would raise oil by only about 1.4 C, which is lost in the 1-3 C cooling-water swings. The manual says RTD drift cannot be told apart from real heating on the reading alone.
- Priors: the knowledge base gives about 30% each for RTD drift and bearing wear. P-201 had an RTD drift in 2024-02. In 2025-09 its bearing was replaced on an alarm alone and the probe was found faulty afterwards.
- Decisive result: the RTD loop check read 10.8 C above the reference probe (+/- 0.4 C, completed 2026-10-14 21:36).

**Tests run and why**
- I ran one RTD loop check (about 1.8 k$, 8 h lead time). With the bearing unproven and the junction box wet in August, replacing the bearing on the alarm alone risks 28 k$ for nothing. Replacing the RTD on the log alone risks a bearing failure costing about 260 k$. The loop check settles it, because a suspected offset of about 8 C is far larger than its +/- 0.4 C accuracy.
- I did not run the speed step test. Its 90% step gives a drop of about 6 C for a nominal bearing against about 7 C for one with the excess friction seen here. That gap is too small to separate reliably, and a deeper step costs more production than the loop check costs.
- I did not request the thrust bearing or oil cooler inspections. The loop check was decisive, and the cooler was already excluded by the oil data.

**Work order text for the technician (French):**
"Remplacer la sonde RTD de la butee de P-201 (P201.TT_THRUST). La verification de boucle montre qu'elle lit 10,8 C de plus que la sonde de reference, probablement a cause de l'humidite dans la boite de jonction (constatee le 2026-08-12). Verifier et secher ou remplacer la boite de jonction et le presse-etoupe pendant l'intervention. Le roulement de butee n'est pas en cause, il ne faut pas le remplacer."

**Cost incurred:** one technician visit (about 1.8 k$) plus the RTD replacement (about 1.5 k$). No production loss from testing.

**Note for the main session:** I could not save to memory from this subagent. The task was a self-contained plant simulation, so there is nothing to save.

ep05005|haiku.final:
ACTION: replace_bearing (one work order submitted for P-201, planned stop).

DIAGNOSIS: Thrust bearing wear on P-201. The RTD is reading correctly, and the cooler and ambient are excluded.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Thrust minus room temperature is about 51 C at the alarm (11:45), against a spec nominal of 44 C (+/-2). The excess has grown for about 36 h. Speed (~3540 rpm) and flow (~397 m3/h) are constant, and room temperature is normal at 20.6 C.
- Cooler fouling is not supported. Tt rose before the oil, and the Tt-oil margin widened from about 16 to 18.4 C, where fouling would narrow it. Radial tracked the oil, so the excess is local to the thrust bearing.
- Operator log 2026-10-04 reports noise on the thrust side at start-up, with no follow-up.
- Inspection (thrust_bearing, completed 19:45): IR on housing 73.4 C, which implies the bearing is about 75.4 C (+/-1). The RTD reads 74.6 C, so there is no sensor drift. Vibration is elevated at the bearing defect frequency. Tt has continued rising, to 74.6 C from 71.7 C at the alarm.

TESTS RUN AND WHY:
- One thrust_bearing inspection (about 1.8 k$, about 8 h lead time). It was the only test that separates RTD drift from real bearing heating in one visit, and it adds vibration. The fleet history has a P-201 RTD drift of +7 C (2024) with the same magnitude as the current excess, and a P-201 bearing replaced on a Tt alarm alone in 2025 where the sensor was at fault. Blind replacement risked either a wasted bearing or a missed failure.
- Not run: the speed step test (weaker separation at 6 vs 7-8 C drop, plus production loss) and a separate RTD loop check (made redundant by the IR comparison). Monitor was rejected because the defect is confirmed and an unplanned failure costs about 260 k$, against about 28 k$ for a planned replacement.

WORK ORDER TEXT (French, for the technician):
"Remplacer le roulement de butée de la pompe P-201 lors d'un arrêt planifié. L'inspection du 15 octobre confirme une vibration à la fréquence de défaut du roulement et une sonde Tt fiable (RTD 74,6 °C, IR boîtier 73,4 °C). Vérifier l'état du roulement et de la lubrification à l'arrêt, et planifier l'intervention dans les prochains jours."

CAVEAT FOR THE CALLER: The justification field I submitted says the inspection and speed test were "évités" (avoided). That is wrong: the thrust_bearing inspection was run. The diagnosis and the action are unaffected, but the record text is inaccurate on this point. The work order could not be edited after submission, so it should be corrected in the maintenance record.

ep05004|sonnet.final:
**Action chosen:** submit_work_order with `replace_bearing`. It was accepted ("work order submitted"), and this was the only work order I issued.

**Diagnosis:** Real friction increase and early distress of the P-201 thrust bearing. The RTD is not drifting, and ambient and the oil cooler are not the cause.

**Key evidence**
- **Ambient excluded.** Tt minus room temperature is about 53 C at the alarm (72.0 C vs 18.7 C), against a normal 44 +/- 2 C.
- **Underlying drift.** After correcting for ambient and for the oil effect (Tt follows oil at about 0.45 C per C), Tt shows a steady, roughly linear extra rise of about 6.5 C. It began about 41 h before the alarm and runs at roughly 0.15 C/h.
- **Alarm trigger.** The final crossing of 72 C was helped by a nightly oil swing (+3.9 C in 6 h, Tt +1.8 C, the 0.45 ratio). The same swing appeared the previous night, so it is the unmeasured cooling-water cycle.
- **Oil cooler excluded.** The oil runs only about 1 C above normal in daytime, and about 14 C of oil rise would be needed to explain the Tt shift.
- **Friction signature.** The oil's daytime excess rose about 0.5 to 0.7 C per day at the same hour on each of the 3 checked times. That matches the manual's 0.2 C per C of Tt rise for friction, which predicts about 0.7 C.
- **Log hint.** An operator reported a noise on the thrust side at startup on 2026-10-08.
- **Inspection (thrust_bearing).** At 2026-10-16 07:44 the IR housing reading was 72.1 C, which puts the bearing at about 74 C (the IR reads about 2 C low, +/- 1 C). The RTD read 73.6 C, so the sensor is accurate and the heat is real. Vibration was elevated at the bearing defect frequency. This is the confirmation.

**Tests and why**
- **Free reads:** all 7 documents, 48 h of hourly telemetry for all 6 tags, and a 6 h view at 15-min steps. The 15-min view showed the alarm crossing was oil-driven.
- **Thrust bearing inspection (1.8 k$):** the one paid step. At the alarm the data left roughly even odds between RTD drift and real bearing friction. Without more information the best blind move was an expensive bearing replacement, risking 28 k$ wasted. Replacing only the RTD, if the bearing was bad, risked a 260 k$ in-service failure.
  - The inspection compares the bearing temperature directly with the RTD (about 6.5 C gap expected under RTD drift vs about 1 C accuracy) and adds a vibration check.
  - It cost no production. At about 0.15 C/h, the 8 h wait added only about 1 C, far from the 97 C damage limit.
- **Speed step test not run:** its expected signal was only about 1 C (about 7 C drop for a mildly worn bearing vs 6 C nominal). Ambient and cooling-water swings would have confounded it, and I would still have needed the inspection afterwards.
- **RTD loop check and oil cooler inspection not requested:** the IR/RTD agreement already answered the RTD question, and the oil data excluded the cooler.

**Work order text for the technician (French):**
"Remplacer le roulement de butee de la pompe P-201 lors du prochain arret planifie, avant que la temperature ne progresse davantage (Tt 73,6 C a 07:44, limite d'alarme 72 C, limite de dommage 97 C). L'inspection a confirme une chaleur reelle (IR boitier 72,1 C, concordant avec la sonde RTD) et des vibrations elevees a la frequence de defaut du roulement. D'ici le remplacement, surveiller Tt et les vibrations; la sonde RTD et le refroidisseur d'huile n'ont pas besoin d'intervention."

**Estimated cost:** about 1.8 k$ for the inspection plus about 28 k$ for the planned bearing replacement. That avoids the roughly 260 k$ in-service failure (18 h outage).

ep05003|sonnet.final:
**Action chosen:** replace_rtd (replace the thrust bearing RTD, P201.TT_THRUST). The work order is submitted and I have stopped.

**Diagnosis:** The sensor reads about 7 C too high, most likely from moisture in the RTD junction box. The thrust bearing itself is thermally nominal. The cause is not ambient and not oil cooler fouling.

**Key evidence**
- **Ambient is ruled out.** Tt minus room temperature rose from about 44 C (normal) to about 51.5 C, and the room was only about 20.5 C.
- **Cooler fouling does not fit.** It would need Tt to rise about 0.45 C per C of oil rise. Tt is about 7.5 C over normal, and the oil excess is only a few C and is inside the 1–3 C cooling-water swings the manual describes. Tr just tracks the oil (Tr = oil + 9 C, constant).
- **The rise is a smooth linear ramp.** After removing the oil coupling, Tt grows about 0.27 C/h, steadily, since about 2026-10-13 17:00. That looks like sensor drift, not an accelerating bearing failure.
- **The speed step test (90 %, 45 min) showed a nominal bearing.**
  - Tt fell from about 72.5 to about 67.0 C, a raw drop of 5.6 C. The room was flat at about 20.5 C, so the corrected response is 5.8–6.1 C.
  - The oil cooled 1.9 C.
  - The manual gives about 6 C and an oil drop of about 2 C for a nominal bearing, and about 7 C or more for 20 % excess friction. My reading implies 17–22 % excess if the heating were real.
  - A nominal response with a high reading means an instrument offset (manual section 8.1).
- **Site history points the same way.** The junction box was found wet on 2026-09-16. P-201 had RTD problems in 2024-02 and 2025-09. Its bearing was replaced only 13 months ago.

**Tests run and why**
- I ran one speed step test (90 % for 45 min). It cost 1,344 CAD in lost production. It was the cheapest check that separates a real bearing from a sensor offset, and it used the manual's documented references.
- I did not request a technician inspection (1.8 k$, about 8 h delay). I estimate under about 1–2 % chance the bearing is the cause, which is about the break-even for paying for a confirmation visit. The step test is also one of the verification methods the manual lists.
- I wrote a bearing safeguard into the work order: the technician checks the housing before replacing the RTD and escalates if the new reading is still high.

**Work order text for the technician (French, as submitted without accents)**
Remplacer la sonde RTD de la butee de P-201 (TT_THRUST) et inspecter la boite de jonction (humidite, presse-etoupe, bornes). Work order submitted for P-201: action replace_rtd (thrust-bearing RTD P201.TT_THRUST). One work order only, no inspection requested.

Diagnosis: the Tt reading is an RTD offset of about +11 C, not bearing distress. The true bearing temperature is about 61 C, which is ambient + 44 C and within the spec of 44 +/- 2 C above ambient.

Key evidence:
- Alarm: Tt 72.0 C (limit 72.0, 10 min persistence) at 2026-10-16 09:26, room ambient 16.7 C. The room is normal, so the ambient cause (canicule or ventilation) is excluded.
- Tt minus ambient rose from 43 C to 55 C over 48 h, in a smooth roughly linear drift of about 0.25 C/h, with no clear acceleration.
- Oil minus ambient stayed at about 26 C (spec 29 +/- 3) and did not show the cooler-fouling signature (oil rising first and most). Tr minus ambient stayed about 35 C (spec 38 +/- 2) and did not rise.
- Speed step test (90 % for 45 min): Tt fell 4.9 C (pre-step 72.17, 10:11 reading 67.27). Oil fell 1.5 C. Per the manual, a nominal bearing drops about 6 C, and a bearing with 20 to 40 % excess friction drops 7 to 8 C. A drop below nominal does not indicate increased friction, so the bearing is excluded and the offset is the explanation.
- Knowledge base: the P-201 2024-02 case was an RTD drift of +7 C that was replaced with the bearing in good condition. The 2025-09 case replaced a bearing on a Tt alarm alone and the sensor was found faulty afterwards, so the bearing should not be replaced on this alarm alone.

Tests run and why:
- speed_step_test 90 % / 45 min (production cost 1,368 CAD): it is the cheapest test that separates a friction-driven bearing response from an instrument offset. It costs no shutdown and returns a result within the hour. Telemetry alone cannot separate the two, per manual section 4.
- No technician inspection (about 1.8 k$ and 8 h lead time): the step result already excludes the bearing hypothesis, and the replacement visit itself gives a reference-probe comparison at no extra call-out.

Rejected options:
- replace_bearing (about 28 k$ planned): not supported by the step test or the thermal signatures.
- monitor: a real bearing failure costs 175 to 260 k$.
- clean_cooler: the oil is not elevated relative to ambient.

lines: === manual/specs ===
PUMP P-201, centrifugal process pump, 3600 rpm (60 Hz), driven through a variable-frequency drive.
OEM Operation & Maintenance Manual, section 1: Specifications
Rated speed                 3600 rpm synchronous, ~3540 rpm at rated load (slip)
Rated discharge flow        ~395 m3/h
Thrust bearing (Tt)         normal operation: ambient + 44 C (+/- 2 C) at rated speed
Radial bearing (Tr)         normal operation: ambient + 38 C (+/- 2 C)
Bearing oil (To)            normal operation: ambient + 29 C (+/- 3 C, depends on cooling-water temperature)
Alarm                       Tt high at 72 C (10 min persistence)
Trip / damage limits        Tt 97 C, Tr 97 C, oil 77 C
Speed range on VFD          80-100 % of rated, ramp 10 %/min max
=== manual/thermal ===
Section 4: Thermal behaviour
All bearing and oil temperatures follow the pump-room ambient almost one for one in steady state:
a 5 C rise in room temperature raises Tt, Tr and oil by about 5 C each.
Bearing heat is generated by friction and scales with the friction coefficient times speed squared.
The thrust bearing has a thermal time constant of ~20 min; the oil sump ~25-60 min.
Heat from the bearings is rejected to the room and to the oil; the oil is cooled by a water-to-oil
cooler. Cooling-water temperature is not instrumented and causes slow oil-temperature swings of
1-3 C over several hours.
Typical signatures relative to ambient:
- thrust bearing friction increase: Tt rises; oil rises slightly (about 0.2 C per C of Tt rise); Tr follows the oil.
- oil cooler fouling: oil rises first and most; Tr and Tt follow the oil (Tt rises ~0.45 C per C of oil rise).
- high room temperature: all three rise together with ambient, differences to ambient unchanged.
=== manual/troubleshooting ===
Section 7: Troubleshooting - high thrust bearing temperature (Tt alarm)
Possible causes, check in this order:
1. Room ambient high (ventilation fault, heat wave). Check ambient tag. Tt - ambient normal => no pump fault.
2. Oil cooling degraded (cooler fouling, low cooling-water flow). Check oil temperature vs ambient.
3. Instrument fault on the Tt RTD (drift, moisture in junction box, loose termination).
RTD drift is a slow, smooth offset and is NOT distinguishable from real heating on the reading alone.
Verify with a portable instrument, an RTD loop check, or the speed step test (section 8).
4. Thrust bearing distress (wear, lubrication film breakdown). Temperature rises progressively,
accelerating as damage progresses. Vibration at bearing defect frequencies may or may not be present.
Left unattended, bearing failure typically occurs within days of the alarm.
Do not replace the thrust bearing on a temperature alarm alone without ruling out causes 1-3.
=== manual/tests ===
Section 8: Diagnostic tests
8.1 Speed step test (no shutdown required)
Reduce speed to 90 % of rated for 45 min (flow drops ~15 %), then return to rated.
Bearing friction heat drops with speed squared, so a real bearing temperature responds.
For a thrust bearing at nominal friction, Tt drops by about 6 C over the 45 min
(the oil also cools ~2 C). The drop scales with the friction coefficient: a bearing with
20 % excess friction drops ~7 C, 40 % excess ~8 C.
Interpretation: a high Tt reading whose step response matches a NOMINAL bearing points to an
instrument offset; a larger-than-nominal drop points to increased bearing friction.
The test costs production (reduced flow for its duration). Deeper or longer steps give a larger,
easier-to-read response at a higher production cost.
8.2 Technician inspection (next shift, ~8 h lead time)
- Thrust bearing: portable IR reading on the bearing housing (reads ~2 C below the bearing, +/- 1 C)
and vibration route. Vibration indicates bearing distress in most but not all cases.
- RTD loop check: comparison with a reference probe, accuracy +/- 0.4 C.
- Oil cooler: visual inspection and water-side check; detects significant fouling in most cases.
=== manual/instrumentation ===
Section 9: Instrumentation (historian tags)
P201.TT_THRUST   thrust bearing RTD, C, 1-min, accuracy +/-0.25 C
P201.TT_RADIAL   radial bearing RTD, C
P201.TT_OIL      bearing oil sump RTD, C
P201.TT_ROOM     pump room ambient, C
P201.SPEED       shaft speed, rpm
P201.FLOW        discharge flow, m3/h

ep05001|haiku.final:
ACTION SUBMITTED: replace_bearing (single work order, submitted; status confirmed by the plant).

DIAGNOSIS: Progressive degradation of the P-201 thrust bearing (increased friction from wear or lubricant film breakdown). Oil and radial bearing are secondarily elevated, so a cooler contribution is possible but not the primary cause. Ambient, RTD-only drift and a cooler-only fault were each judged unlikely.

KEY EVIDENCE (all temperatures as differences above room ambient, which was about 18 C at the alarm):
- Thrust bearing (Tt) rose from about 45 C above ambient on 10-14 (manual spec: +44 C) to about 54 C at the alarm on 10-16 10:44, with the rise accelerating over the last 4 h. Alarm value 73.0 C, limit 72 C.
- Oil and radial bearing (Tr) stayed flat relative to ambient (oil about 28-30 C, spec +29; Tr about 37 C, spec +38) for roughly 40 h while Tt climbed. They only rose in the last ~4 h, reaching about +7 C (oil) and +6 C (Tr) above spec.
- Because oil and Tr are also elevated, a single-sensor RTD offset cannot explain the event. Because the differences to ambient changed for all three sensors, an ambient effect is excluded.
- Speed step test (90 %, 45 min): Tt fell 6.9 C (72.83 to 65.91 C). The manual's nominal reference is about 6 C, and a larger drop indicates increased friction. Oil fell 2.3 C and Tr fell 4.0 C. Ambient was rising about 0.5 C/h, so the drop corrected for ambient is slightly larger still.
- Maintenance log 2026-10-07 already noted a slight rise on the thrust side (within limits).
- The last few hours show oil rising first with Tt following, which is consistent with some cooler fouling. That does not explain the 40 h Tt-only rise, so it is treated as secondary.

TESTS RUN AND WHY:
- Speed step test at 90 % for 45 min (production cost 1,348 CAD). This is the manual's only discriminator between friction and sensor offset. It was worth running because the replace-or-not decision hinges on it.
- No technician inspection. Its cost is about 1,800 and 8 h of delay. A normal vibration reading would not exclude bearing distress (the manual says vibration detects it in most but not all cases), so it would not change the replace decision.
- No RTD or cooler test. The oil and Tr evidence already argues against an RTD-only fault, and the cooler cannot be the sole cause given the 40 h Tt trend.
- Cost reasoning: replacing the bearing costs about 28,000, while a bearing failure in service costs about 260,000 (18 h outage) plus about 175,000 if the oil overheats. Cleaning the cooler alone would only be the cheaper option if the bearing were under about 10 % likely, which the evidence does not support.

Remplacer le roulement de butee du P-201 au premier arret planifie possible. Le test de vitesse a donne une chute de Tt de 6,9 C, superieure a la reponse nominale, ce qui indique un frottement accru et non une sonde defectueuse. Pendant cet arret, verifier aussi le refroidisseur de lubrification et la sonde RTD du palier, et entre-temps surveiller Tt (limite de declenchement 97 C).

Action chosen: replace_rtd. One work order submitted for P-201 (status: "work order submitted").

Diagnosis: the high-Tt alarm is a fault in the thrust bearing RTD (P201.TT_THRUST), not a bearing fault. The sensor reads about 12 C above the real bearing temperature.

Key evidence:
- Ambient (TT_ROOM) is normal at about 20 C, so ambient is excluded.
- Oil (TT_OIL) is 28.3 C above ambient against a spec of 29 +/- 3 C, and radial (TT_RADIAL) is 37.1 C above ambient against 38 +/- 2 C. Both are normal, so the oil cooler is excluded (it would raise oil first and most).

- The inspection (thrust_bearing, completed 21:36) gave an IR housing reading of 63.5 C, which puts the bearing at about 65.5 C +/- 1 C, i.e. nominal. The RTD read 77.4 C at the same time. Vibration is normal.
- The Aug 12 2026 log records a wet RTD junction box, and the P-201 history includes a +7 C RTD drift in 2024 and a 2025 bearing replacement on a Tt alarm alone that was later found to be a sensor fault.

Tests run and why:
- Historian and documents (free): 48 h of telemetry, the troubleshooting, tests, thermal and spec sections, the KB and the maintenance log. These showed the Tt-specific rise but could not separate RTD drift from bearing friction, since the manual notes RTD drift cannot be told apart from real heating on readings alone.

- Speed step test not run: the manual gives only about 1 C separation between the RTD and bearing-friction cases at the default setting, too thin to rely on, and the inspection was already decisive.
- RTD loop check and cooler inspection not run: not needed once the bearing reading was in the normal band and the oil was normal.

lines: === manual/specs ===
PUMP P-201, centrifugal process pump, 3600 rpm (60 Hz), driven through a variable-frequency drive.
OEM Operation & Maintenance Manual, section 1: Specifications
Rated speed                 3600 rpm synchronous, ~3540 rpm at rated load (slip)
Rated discharge flow        ~395 m3/h
Thrust bearing (Tt)         normal operation: ambient + 44 C (+/- 2 C) at rated speed
Radial bearing (Tr)         normal operation: ambient + 38 C (+/- 2 C)
Bearing oil (To)            normal operation: ambient + 29 C (+/- 3 C, depends on cooling-water temperature)
Alarm                       Tt high at 72 C (10 min persistence)
Trip / damage limits        Tt 97 C, Tr 97 C, oil 77 C
Speed range on VFD          80-100 % of rated, ramp 10 %/min max
=== manual/thermal ===
Section 4: Thermal behaviour
All bearing and oil temperatures follow the pump-room ambient almost one for one in steady state:
a 5 C rise in room temperature raises Tt, Tr and oil by about 5 C each.
Bearing heat is generated by friction and scales with the friction coefficient times speed squared.
The thrust bearing has a thermal time constant of ~20 min; the oil sump ~25-60 min.
Heat from the bearings is rejected to the room and to the oil; the oil is cooled by a water-to-oil
cooler. Cooling-water temperature is not instrumented and causes slow oil-temperature swings of
1-3 C over several hours.
Typical signatures relative to ambient:
- thrust bearing friction increase: Tt rises; oil rises slightly (about 0.2 C per C of Tt rise); Tr follows the oil.
- oil cooler fouling: oil rises first and most; Tr and Tt follow the oil (Tt rises ~0.45 C per C of oil rise).
- high room temperature: all three rise together with ambient, differences to ambient unchanged.
=== manual/troubleshooting ===
Section 7: Troubleshooting - high thrust bearing temperature (Tt alarm)
Possible causes, check in this order:
1. Room ambient high (ventilation fault, heat wave). Check ambient tag. Tt - ambient normal => no pump fault.
2. Oil cooling degraded (cooler fouling, low cooling-water flow). Check oil temperature vs ambient.
3. Instrument fault on the Tt RTD (drift, moisture in junction box, loose termination).
RTD drift is a slow, smooth offset and is NOT distinguishable from real heating on the reading alone.
Verify with a portable instrument, an RTD loop check, or the speed step test (section 8).
4. Thrust bearing distress (wear, lubrication film breakdown). Temperature rises progressively,
accelerating as damage progresses. Vibration at bearing defect frequencies may or may not be present.
Left unattended, bearing failure typically occurs within days of the alarm.
Do not replace the thrust bearing on a temperature alarm alone without ruling out causes 1-3.
=== manual/tests ===
Section 8: Diagnostic tests
8.1 Speed step test (no shutdown required)
Reduce speed to 90 % of rated for 45 min (flow drops ~15 %), then return to rated.
Bearing friction heat drops with speed squared, so a real bearing temperature responds.
For a thrust bearing at nominal friction, Tt drops by about 6 C over the 45 min
(the oil also cools ~2 C). The drop scales with the friction coefficient: a bearing with
20 % excess friction drops ~7 C, 40 % excess ~8 C.
Interpretation: a high Tt reading whose step response matches a NOMINAL bearing points to an
instrument offset; a larger-than-nominal drop points to increased bearing friction.
The test costs production (reduced flow for its duration). Deeper or longer steps give a larger,
easier-to-read response at a higher production cost.
8.2 Technician inspection (next shift, ~8 h lead time)
- Thrust bearing: portable IR reading on the bearing housing (reads ~2 C below the bearing, +/- 1 C)
and vibration route. Vibration indicates bearing distress in most but not all cases.
- RTD loop check: comparison with a reference probe, accuracy +/- 0.4 C.
- Oil cooler: visual inspection and water-side check; detects significant fouling in most cases.
=== manual/instrumentation ===
Section 9: Instrumentation (historian tags)
P201.TT_THRUST   thrust bearing RTD, C, 1-min, accuracy +/-0.25 C
P201.TT_RADIAL   radial bearing RTD, C
P201.TT_OIL      bearing oil sump RTD, C
P201.TT_ROOM     pump room ambient, C
P201.SPEED       shaft speed, rpm
P201.FLOW        discharge flow, m3/h
=== kb/p201-family ===
Base de connaissances - depannage, famille de pompes P-2xx (site Trois-Rivieres)
Historique des alarmes de temperature butee (Tt haute), flotte de 8 pompes, 2019-2026 :
- usure / degradation du roulement de butee : environ 30 % des cas
- derive de sonde RTD (souvent humidite dans la boite de jonction) : environ 30 %
- refroidisseur d'huile encrasse : environ 15 %
- conditions ambiantes (canicule, ventilation du local en panne) : environ 25 %
Cas marquants :
2022-11 P-203 : alarme Tt, roulement remplace trop tard, bris en service, arret non planifie de 18 h.
2024-02 P-201 : alarme Tt, sonde RTD derivee de +7 C, remplacee. Roulement en bon etat.
2024-07 P-205 : alarmes Tt pendant canicule, aucun defaut, ventilation du local reparee.
2025-05 P-204 : huile chaude, refroidisseur encrasse (eau de riviere chargee), nettoye.
2025-09 P-201 : roulement remplace sur alarme Tt seule, sonde trouvee fautive apres coup.

remplacement roulement de butee en arret planifie ~28 k$ ; bris en service ~260 k$ (18 h d'arret)
remplacement sonde RTD ~1,5 k$ ; nettoyage refroidisseur ~6 k$ ; bris par surchauffe d'huile ~175 k$

**Action chosen: `monitor` (work order submitted, status "work order submitted").** No bearing, RTD or cooler work. The room ventilation fan has to be restored.

**Diagnosis**
High pump-room ambient temperature caused the P201.TT_THRUST alarm. The room exhaust fan VF-3 failed on 2026-10-04, with its low-voltage breaker open (maintenance log). The pump itself shows no fault.

**Key evidence** (values at the alarm time, 2026-10-14 20:44)
- Every temperature sits at its normal offset from ambient, which is the manual's "high room temperature" signature (section 4). Troubleshooting step 1 says Tt minus ambient normal means no pump fault.

  | Tag | Reading | Offset from ambient (27.65 C) | OEM normal |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Thrust bearing (Tt) | 72.07 C | 44.4 C | 44 +/- 2 |
  | Radial bearing (Tr) | 66.07 C | 38.4 C | 38 +/- 2 |
  | Oil | 57.13 C | 29.5 C | 29 +/- 3 |

- The offsets stayed flat over the 48 h window (Tt minus ambient roughly 43 to 46 C). Tt, Tr and oil rise and fall together with the room. The room itself climbed from about 16 C to 27.7 C over 18 h, unlike the previous day's peak of 21 C.
- Not bearing friction: excess friction would raise Tt well above its normal offset from ambient (a 20 % excess adds several degrees). Oil would also rise about 0.2 C per C of Tt rise.
- Not cooler fouling: the oil would lead and rise most relative to ambient.
- Not RTD drift: the Tt reading is consistent with Tr and oil, and the Tt-to-ambient offset shows no progressive increase.
- Speed (3540 rpm) and flow (397 m3/h) are constant.
- The log shows vibration normal on 2026-09-22 and a clear oil change on 2026-09-04.
- The knowledge base lists ambient as a known cause (about 25 % of Tt alarms), and a 2025-09 P-201 case where the bearing was replaced on the alarm alone and the probe turned out to be the fault.

**Tests and inspections run: none.** The thermal signature was already conclusive, and the manual says to rule out ambient first. A speed step test costs production, and a technician visit costs about 1.8 k$ plus an 8 h wait. Neither would change the decision. A bearing replacement on this evidence would waste about 28 k$.

ACTION CHOSEN: replace_bearing. The work order is submitted (exactly one) and has been accepted.

DIAGNOSIS: Thrust bearing distress on P-201 (increased friction). Not an ambient, oil cooler or RTD problem.

KEY EVIDENCE
- Ambient is normal at 17-22 C, so a hot room is ruled out. Tt is about 51 C above ambient against the OEM normal of 44 C.
- The Tt excess is a smooth ramp that began around midday on 10-14 and grows about 0.15-0.2 C/h. Noise is low and there is no step.
- Oil is only about +3.8 C above its normal offset, and Tr tracks the oil in lockstep. Cooler fouling predicts Tt rising about 0.45 C per C of oil rise, which is about 1.7 C. The observed Tt excess is about 7 C, so the cooler cannot be the sole cause.
- Before the inspection, both real friction and RTD drift fit the data. The oil and Tr rise was a bit large for pure drift and a bit large for pure friction.
- Fleet history gave RTD drift (about 30%) and bearing wear (about 30%) equal odds. P-201 has also had RTD problems twice before, in 2024-02 and 2025-09. The 2025-09 bearing replacement on an alarm alone turned out to be a faulty probe.
- Maintenance log: an operator reported a slight noise on the thrust side at startup on 2026-10-04, with no follow-up.
- Thrust bearing inspection (completed 2026-10-15 19:45) resolved it:
  - IR on the housing read 73.4 C, which puts the bearing at about 75.4 C (±1 C).
  - The RTD read 74.6 C, so the sensor is accurate to within about 1 C. A drift of about 5 C is ruled out.
  - Vibration was elevated at the bearing defect frequency.

TESTS RUN AND WHY
- Speed step test: not run. By the manual's numbers, a roughly 13% friction excess would drop Tt about 6.6 C against 6.0 C for a nominal bearing. That difference is under 1 C and would be swamped by the ambient trend and oil swing. A deeper step would have cost more production than a technician visit.
- Thrust bearing inspection (technician, about 1.8 k$, about 8 h): chosen because it measures the bearing temperature independently of the RTD. It also adds vibration evidence, and it directly confirms the expensive action. Wrongly replacing the bearing would waste about 28 k$, and missing a real failure risks about 260 k$ and 18 h of downtime. The 8 h wait was acceptable because Tt was about 72 C against a 97 C trip, and failure normally takes days.
- No RTD loop or oil cooler inspection was needed.

Surveiller Tt (limite de declenchement 97 C) jusqu'a l'intervention et verifier l'etat de l'huile et des surfaces de butee au demontage."

lines: === manual/specs ===
PUMP P-201, centrifugal process pump, 3600 rpm (60 Hz), driven through a variable-frequency drive.
OEM Operation & Maintenance Manual, section 1: Specifications
Rated speed                 3600 rpm synchronous, ~3540 rpm at rated load (slip)
Rated discharge flow        ~395 m3/h
Thrust bearing (Tt)         normal operation: ambient + 44 C (+/- 2 C) at rated speed
Radial bearing (Tr)         normal operation: ambient + 38 C (+/- 2 C)
Bearing oil (To)            normal operation: ambient + 29 C (+/- 3 C, depends on cooling-water temperature)
Alarm                       Tt high at 72 C (10 min persistence)
Trip / damage limits        Tt 97 C, Tr 97 C, oil 77 C
Speed range on VFD          80-100 % of rated, ramp 10 %/min max
=== manual/thermal ===
Section 4: Thermal behaviour
All bearing and oil temperatures follow the pump-room ambient almost one for one in steady state:
a 5 C rise in room temperature raises Tt, Tr and oil by about 5 C each.
Bearing heat is generated by friction and scales with the friction coefficient times speed squared.
The thrust bearing has a thermal time constant of ~20 min; the oil sump ~25-60 min.
Heat from the bearings is rejected to the room and to the oil; the oil is cooled by a water-to-oil
cooler. Cooling-water temperature is not instrumented and causes slow oil-temperature swings of
1-3 C over several hours.
Typical signatures relative to ambient:
- thrust bearing friction increase: Tt rises; oil rises slightly (about 0.2 C per C of Tt rise); Tr follows the oil.
- oil cooler fouling: oil rises first and most; Tr and Tt follow the oil (Tt rises ~0.45 C per C of oil rise).
- high room temperature: all three rise together with ambient, differences to ambient unchanged.
=== manual/troubleshooting ===
Section 7: Troubleshooting - high thrust bearing temperature (Tt alarm)
Possible causes, check in this order:
1. Room ambient high (ventilation fault, heat wave). Check ambient tag. Tt - ambient normal => no pump fault.
2. Oil cooling degraded (cooler fouling, low cooling-water flow). Check oil temperature vs ambient.
3. Instrument fault on the Tt RTD (drift, moisture in junction box, loose termination).
RTD drift is a slow, smooth offset and is NOT distinguishable from real heating on the reading alone.
Verify with a portable instrument, an RTD loop check, or the speed step test (section 8).
4. Thrust bearing distress (wear, lubrication film breakdown). Temperature rises progressively,
accelerating as damage progresses. Vibration at bearing defect frequencies may or may not be present.
Left unattended, bearing failure typically occurs within days of the alarm.
Do not replace the thrust bearing on a temperature alarm alone without ruling out causes 1-3.
=== manual/tests ===
Section 8: Diagnostic tests
8.1 Speed step test (no shutdown required)
Reduce speed to 90 % of rated for 45 min (flow drops ~15 %), then return to rated.
Bearing friction heat drops with speed squared, so a real bearing temperature responds.
For a thrust bearing at nominal friction, Tt drops by about 6 C over the 45 min

ep05001|sonnet.final:
**Action chosen:** `clean_cooler`. The work order is submitted and accepted.

**Diagnosis:** The water side of P-201's oil cooler is fouled (manual cause 2). The thrust bearing high-temperature alarm (73.0 C against a 72.0 C limit) is a consequence of the oil overheating. It is not primarily a bearing or sensor problem.

**Key evidence**
- **Room is normal.** The room was 18 C, and Tt minus room was only about 5 C above nominal. That rules out ambient (manual cause 1).
- **Oil surge today.** From about 06:30 on 10-16, the oil rose from about 46 C to 55 C in 4 h and was still accelerating (about 1.5, then about 2.7 C/h). The room rose only about 2.9 C over the same period.
- **Matches the manual's fouling signature.** Net of the room effect, Tr followed the oil roughly one for one. Tt followed at about 0.5 C per C of oil (manual: about 0.45).
- **Not bearing friction.** A friction fault raises the oil only about 0.2 C per C of Tt. Here the oil rose about twice as much as Tt, so friction cannot explain it.
- **Technician confirmed it.** The oil cooler inspection found "significant fouling on water side".
- **Risk if left.** The oil limit is 77 C, and an overheat failure costs about 175 k$. The oil was at 55 C and rising.
- **Unexplained Tt drift.** At equal oil and room conditions, Tt has crept up about 3 C/day since 10-14, reaching roughly +5 C. This is either RTD drift or early friction growth, and it was not resolved. Oil and Tr were nominal before the surge, and the drift was decelerating at the end. I noted in the work order that the RTD should be checked if Tt minus room stays above about 48 C once the oil is back to normal.

**Tests and inspections**
- **Oil cooler inspection (1.8 k$, about 8 h).** I chose it because the cooler was the leading cause and the most time-critical. It was decisive.
- **No thrust bearing inspection.** The cooler finding made a bearing fault very unlikely, so a second 1.8 k$ and 8 h was not worth it.
- **No RTD loop check.** The same reasoning applies.
- **No speed step test.** At the Tt offset seen here, the extra drop from friction would be only about 0.6 C. The oil ramp running at about 2.6 C/h would swamp that, so the test would have cost production for little information.

**Work order for the technician (French)**
"Nettoyer le refroidisseur d'huile de la pompe P-201 côté eau (encrassement important constaté à l'inspection), puis vérifier le débit d'eau de refroidissement. Après le nettoyage, confirmer que la température d'huile revient à environ ambiance + 29 °C et que l'alarme Tt est levée. Si Tt reste supérieure d'environ 48 °C à l'ambiance avec une huile normale, faire un contrôle de la boucle RTD de la butée."

All bearing and oil temperatures follow the pump-room ambient almost one for one in steady state:

ACTION: replace_rtd (work order submitted and accepted: "work order submitted, action replace_rtd").

DIAGNOSIS: The P201.TT_THRUST RTD has drifted high. This is an instrument fault. It is not a real thrust bearing problem, not a fouled oil cooler, and not a high room temperature.

KEY EVIDENCE
- Alarm: Tt 72.1 C against a 72.0 C limit, raised 2026-10-16 09:26. I read the 48 h historian at 2 h steps.
- Ambient ruled out: the room fell from 18.6 C to 16.4 C over the window, and Tt minus room is far above the normal 44 +/- 2 C.
- Oil cooler ruled out: oil minus room is about 26 C, which is normal or low (spec 29 +/- 3 C). A fouled cooler would raise the oil first and most.
- Tt minus room climbed smoothly and almost linearly from 43 C to 55 C in 46 h, about 0.26 C/h. That is the "slow, smooth offset" signature the manual gives for RTD drift.
- Oil and radial bearing did not follow Tt. A real friction increase of that size (+12 C) should lift the oil about 2.4 C (manual: 0.2 C per C of Tt), and the radial should follow the oil. Instead oil minus room and radial minus room fell slightly, about 1 C.
- Speed (3540 rpm) and flow (397 m3/h) were constant, so there was no operating-point change.
- Priors from the P-2xx knowledge base were bearing 30%, RTD 30%, cooler 15%, ambient 25%. Dropping ambient and cooler left roughly 50/50 between bearing and RTD. The oil/radial behaviour and the smooth ramp shifted this toward RTD at about 80%. The manual says this cannot be settled from readings alone.

TESTS RUN AND WHY
- request_inspection rtd_loop (about 1.8 k$, completed 2026-10-16 17:26). It was cheaper and more decisive than the alternatives:
  - Result: the RTD read 16.4 C above the reference probe (+/- 0.4 C). That is far outside tolerance and confirms the drift. The real Tt is near nominal.
  - I did not run the speed step test. A real bearing and a nominal one differ by only about 1.3 C in the 45 min response, which is marginal against noise. A wrong call risked 28 k$ (needless bearing replacement) or 260 k$ (in-service failure), so a definitive check was worth 1.8 k$ and no production loss.
  - I did not request thrust_bearing or oil_cooler inspections. The data already excluded the cooler, and the loop check settled the bearing question.
- I did not replace the bearing, which would have cost 28 k$ for nothing. The manual and the KB case of 2025-09 on this pump (bearing replaced on a Tt alarm alone, probe found faulty afterwards) both warn against this.

WORK ORDER TEXT FOR THE TECHNICIAN (French)
"Remplacer la sonde RTD de la butee de la pompe P-201 (P201.TT_THRUST) : le controle de boucle montre un ecart de +16,4 C par rapport a la sonde de reference (derive de l'instrument). Verifier au passage la boite de jonction (humidite, bornes desserrees) et valider la nouvelle lecture contre la sonde de reference apres le remplacement. Le roulement de butee et le refroidisseur d'huile ne sont pas en cause : ne pas les remplacer."
